thread:
oncall-bot: PAGER: severity=high — Smart-routing control plane detected repeated fallback loops during canary rollout for model 'chat-lite-v2' across us-west and eu-west. Error pattern: sticky-fallback rebinds to failing variant. Paging oncall.
Alex Chen: saw this on the dashboard, spikes in 5xx when canary weight at ~10% and sticky routing enabled. Prefetch cache misses too.
Maya R: digging into routing logs now. looks like canary instances in us-west hit OOM and returned 502, traffic fell back to old-variant but sticky cookie TTL was long so repeated rebinds kept hitting failing canary after healthcheck windows expired.
Priya K: tagging SRE. Alex, can you confirm which rollout policy was used? canary + sticky-fallback? any manual overrides?
Alex Chen: rollout config is rollout:v2 -> canaryTraffic=10%, fallback=sticky, fallback_ttl=3600s. no manual overrides in console. deploy-bot shows canary started ~06:42 UTC.
Oliver S: past incidents we saw sticky+long TTL cause oscillation if healthchecks are slow. Suggest pause rollout and move fallback to immediate ephemeral fallback while we fix canary.
Alex Chen: initiating pause now. deploy-bot: /rollout pause chat-lite-v2 -> acknowledged. Pausing reduced canary decisions but existing sticky tokens still in circuit.
Maya R: sharing logs:
```
routing: bind request id=ae12 -> variant=canary
healthcheck: canary/instance-7 status=unhealthy (OOM)
fallback: sticky-bind token=st_98a -> rebind to variant=canary after 20s
```
Maya R: looks like rebinds happen when the LB retries; sticky token TTL override logic picks highest-affinity variant even if unhealthy because health state hadn't propagated.
Priya K: risk assessment — customer-facing errors: yes, ~2.1% of requests in us-west got 5xx in last 6m. Biggest impact on interactive chat product. CS notified.
Karen L: confirmed CS alert: 4 enterprise customers reported degraded generation latency and intermittent failures. asked for mitigation ETA.
Alex Chen: mitigation plan: 1) set fallback policy to ephemeral for the route; 2) invalidate sticky tokens for recent canary cohort; 3) roll back canary if we see persistent OOM. executing step 1 now.
Maya R: policy change command:
```
PATCH /routes/chat-lite/traffic
{
  "fallback_policy": "ephemeral",
  "sticky_ttl": 30
}
```
deploy-bot: policy update applied by Alex Chen at 06:58 UTC — changes propagated to control plane.
Alex Chen: running script to evict sticky tokens for cohort tag=canary-210512
```
evict-sticky --cohort canary-210512 --force
```
Oliver S: evict confirmed on control plane — tokens removed from cache nodes. routing logs now show fallback to stable variant reliably.
Maya R: monitoring metrics: 5xx rate dropping from 2.1% -> 0.4% over 3 minutes. latency normalizing. rolling window shows gradual recovery.
Priya K: are we confident to resume canary with fix? what's root cause — OOM on instance-7 maybe due to newer attention kernel memory spike.
Maya R: hypothesis: model var binary has a memory regression under long-sequence tails. we'll reproduce in staging with identical batch sizes + kv-cache sizes.
Alex Chen: action items: A) roll back canary binary to v1.9 and retest; B) run mem profile on canary in staging; C) add control-plane guard: if fallback oscillation > X in 5m, auto-pause rollout and set fallback=ephemeral.
Karen L: CS update sent: "Mitigation in place, stable variant serving while we investigate. We will follow up with root cause and timeline." customers acknowledged.
Priya K: long-term: consider TTL upper bound on sticky cookies per rollout and health-propagation fastpath where unhealthy variant loses affinity immediately.
Maya R: filed ticket INF-8721 for mem regression; attaching heap dumps and kernel trace. tagging runtime team.
Oliver S: after eviction steady-state looks good. Recommend keeping canary paused until we validate memory profile — set status to 'paused:investigating'.
Alex Chen: setting rollout state -> paused:investigating. deploy-bot: rollout state updated.
Priya K: I'll create post-incident follow-ups and schedule hotfix window. thanks team. moving to postmortem channel after this thread. :white_check_mark:
